text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty PAGER fired: `dedicated-gpu-pool-502-rate` (threshold breach). auto-triggered at 03:12 UTC

pagerduty: Pager duty note: Incident triggered by 5 consecutive 502s from runtime proxies to dedicated pools. Auto-notify to oncall.

maria: acked. looking now. any customer impact reported?

james: seeing a 10x spike in 502 rate from proxies -> runtime in us-west-2 for model-pool:d24. Traffic pattern looks bursty from 3 external clients (suspect large batching job).

anya: confirmed logs show `upstream_response_time` spikes and `error: upstream reset`. redis KV errors spike too around same window.

maria: quick check: only 6 dedicated endpoints affected (~2% of dedicated traffic). No wide-hosted API impact so far. opening k8s events for the affected nodes.

james: paste logs snippet:
```
[03:11:58] proxy->runtime: POST /v1/generate 502 upstream reset (conn_id=5982)
[03:11:59] runtime: KV cache miss flood, OOM-evict candidate: model-d24 shard-3
[03:12:01] autoscaler: scale-down inhibited, pending eviction
```

pagerduty: PagerDuty auto-ack window expired, escalating to L2 after 3 minutes.

maria: trying a quick mitigation: disabling aggressive batching on the affected pool and enabling prefix KV warmup. applying config now: `--batch-size=8 -> 4`, `kv-prefetch=true`

anya: applied. pushing config hash `cfg-2026-03-15-03a`.

incident-bot: Action applied: runtime config update succeeded (deploy id cfg-2026-03-15-03a).

pd-bot: PagerDuty update: alert auto-resolved (brief drop below threshold) at 03:14 UTC.

james: it's back down to baseline for 90s, but looks like it flapped. still seeing occasional 502s tailing.

maria: re-opened traces for the 03:12-03:15 window, correlating client IDs. One client shows a sudden QPS jump and large payloads. sent them a DM to ask about a deploy.

pagerduty: PagerDuty: alert refired at 03:16 UTC (same rule). Auto-repeat detected.

anya: re-run heap and network checks on the few runtime nodes. CPU ok, but network retransmits higher. Kernel dropped packets on one node (eni flapping suspicion).

maria: moving traffic away from node-17 with `maintenance` tag to test. routing-change: `route: node-17 -> drain`.

incident-bot: Routing change initiated; rebalancer in progress.

james: while rebalancer runs, I'm enabling fallback-model-route for the busiest customer to reduce load on the heavy model. this will route them to a quantized variant with lower memory usage.

pd-bot: PagerDuty: after routing change, alert auto-resolved again at 03:18 UTC (short window).

maria: observation: each mitigation briefly clears the spike then it returns when the client retries aggressively. looks like client backoff is missing.

anya: recommended short-term WAF/QoS throttle for client-id: CUST-998 to cap burst qps to 20/s. raised a temporary rule.

james: QoS rule in place. also bumped dedicated-pool eviction threshold to avoid cascading evictions during short bursts.

pagerduty: PagerDuty: alert fired again at 03:21 UTC (third occurrence). This is now creating a flapping pattern, auto-resolve cycles observed. Escalation to L2 acknowledged.

maria: ok leaving a sticky note: oncall handoff plan if this keeps flapping — call SRE war room and route to night oncall leo.

leo: joining channel (oncall takeover at 03:25 UTC). briefed. what still open?

maria: current status: small subset of dedicated endpoints in us-west showing intermittent 502s correlated with client CUST-998 bursty large payloads; mitigations applied: reduce batch size, enable kv-prefetch, drain node-17, enable fallback model variant, QoS throttle for client. each mitigation gives temporary relief then pagerduty re-fires. no broad customer outage, isolated but noisy.

leo: thanks — I'll keep the throttle and monitor. propose adding a short term circuit breaker that rejects requests over 30s payload size for that pool and adds a 5s backoff header instructing clients. can we push that quickly?

james: I can push a filter on the edge proxy to reject huge payloads with 413 and `Retry-After: 5`. prepping patch now.

incident-bot: Patch queued: `edge-filter/payload-size-limit-5mb`. will deploy in 60s.

pd-bot: PagerDuty: alert auto-resolved at 03:26 UTC after edge filter starts taking effect.

maria: monitoring metrics: 502 rate down to baseline for 10+ mins. reduced re-fires. good candidate for follow-up.

leo: I'll own the postmortem and coordinate with product to inform the affected customer. immediate next steps: 1) confirm client deploy/change, 2) permanent QoS or backoff enforcement, 3) revisit autoscaler thresholds to avoid over-eager evictions.

james: logging follow-up: add clearer logs for `upstream reset` with client-id + payload-size to speed future triage.

anya: I'll file a quick incident ticket and label as `flapping-autoresolve-dedicated-502` for org tracking.

maria: thanks team. handing off to leo for overnight watch. if it flaps again, escalate to SRE war room.

leo: acknowledged. handing off to night rotation. I'll update PD to squash repeated auto-resolves (adjusting dedupe) so it doesn't spam.

incident-bot: Thread note: final state at 03:32 UTC — mitigations stabilized, participants: maria, james, anya, leo. follow-up: ticket INC-2026-1423 created.

maria: thx all. :thumbsup:
